title: Curvefield — Elliptic-Curve Cryptography Lab
description: An interactive ECC lab: the geometric group law, finite-field curves, a from-scratch secp256k1 cryptosystem (ECDSA + BIP-340 Schnorr + MuSig2), Curve25519, and a hand-written BLS12-381 pairing — now standards-grade and the substrate for a from-scratch Groth16 zk-SNARK. RFC 9380 hash-to-curve (expand_message_xmd, Simplified SWU with the 11-/3-isogenies, cofactor clearing) reproduces the RFC's own G1/G2 test vectors; ZCash/Ethereum point serialization, IRTF BLS signatures with HKDF KeyGen (matching the EIP-2333 vector) and proof-of-possession, and an optimized Hayashida–Aranha final exponentiation round out a production-shaped pairing stack. The Groth16 lab proves knowledge of a secret (x³+x+5=out) in three group elements, verified by one pairing equation, and a from-scratch PLONK lab proves the *same* statement with a universal setup — selector-gate arithmetization, a copy-constraint permutation argument, a grand-product polynomial, and a transparent KZG-batched verifier — so the two SNARKs sit side by side. From-scratch BULLETPROOFS add a Fiat–Shamir inner-product argument that folds the witness in half each round, giving aggregated logarithmic range proofs (a 64-bit amount in ~16 group elements, ~20× smaller than the linear form) checked by both a transparent and an optimized single-multiexp verifier, plus a full confidential transaction — homomorphic kernel-excess balance over an aggregated range proof, the Monero/Mimblewimble structure, with an inflation attack shown to break it. Plus Schnorr adaptor signatures and atomic swaps, BIP-32 HD wallets, Shamir/Feldman secret sharing, FROST threshold signatures, zero-knowledge Σ-protocols (Pedersen, Chaum–Pedersen, range proofs), KZG polynomial commitments, and discrete-log + invalid-curve attacks. A from-scratch STARK rounds out the proof-system shelf: the one system here that needs no elliptic curve and no trusted setup — transparent and plausibly post-quantum, resting on a hash alone. It proves an actual execution (a Fibonacci-square recurrence) over the Goldilocks field p = 2⁶⁴ − 2³² + 1 with a hand-written NTT, Merkle commitments, a Fiat–Shamir transcript, DEEP out-of-domain sampling, and a full FRI low-degree test — and demonstrates soundness live by rejecting a forged intermediate step. A VERIFIABLE RANDOM FUNCTION lab implements ECVRF (RFC 9381) on Edwards25519 in both ciphersuites — try-and-increment and the constant-time Elligator2 map — reproducing the RFC's own proof (π) test vectors byte-for-byte and driving a verifiable leader-election lottery. A LINKABLE RING SIGNATURE lab builds Monero's anonymity core from scratch — SAG, bLSAG, and the concise CLSAG with key images I = x·Hₚ(P), plus CryptoNote stealth one-time addresses — assembled into a complete private payment that hides the sender yet still catches a double-spend. A SEALED secure-channel lab closes the one missing dimension — confidentiality — by assembling the whole engine into the SIGNAL PROTOCOL, the end-to-end encryption behind WhatsApp and Signal: a from-scratch ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439, pinned byte-for-byte), HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869), XEdDSA prekey signatures, X3DH key agreement with an offline recipient, and the Double Ratchet that gives every message forward secrecy and heals the session one round trip after a full key compromise — driven by a live Alice⇄Bob chat you can tamper with, reorder, and compromise. A POST-QUANTUM lattice lab adds ML-KEM (FIPS 203, the standardised CRYSTALS-Kyber) built entirely from scratch — a hand-written Keccak/SHA-3 + SHAKE sponge (pinned to the FIPS 202 digests), the negacyclic number-theoretic transform over Z₃₃₂₉[X]/(X²⁵⁶+1) with a base multiply pinned to a schoolbook convolution, centered-binomial noise, Compress/Decompress ciphertext coding, and the Fujisaki–Okamoto transform with implicit rejection — for all three parameter sets (ML-KEM-512/768/1024), matching the standard's key and ciphertext byte-sizes exactly and demonstrating IND-CCA2 by catching a mauled ciphertext; wired into the real TLS 1.3 X25519MLKEM768 hybrid handshake so a classical curve and a lattice KEM secure one session together. Its companion, ML-DSA (FIPS 204, the standardised CRYSTALS-Dilithium), completes the post-quantum story with the mainstream lattice SIGNATURE that retires ECDSA/Ed25519/BLS — a from-scratch Fiat–Shamir-with-aborts scheme over Z₈₃₈₀₄₁₇[X]/(X²⁵⁶+1): a full 256-point NTT (the ring splits completely), Power2Round/Decompose and the MakeHint/UseHint carry-recovery mechanism (each pinned by its round-trip identity), the ExpandA/ExpandS/ExpandMask samplers and the τ-sparse SampleInBall challenge, byte-exact packing with a validating hint decoder, and the rejection-sampling signing loop that keeps the response independent of the secret — for all three parameter sets (ML-DSA-44/65/87), matching the standard's exact key and signature byte-sizes and rejecting any tampered message, mauled signature, or wrong key, with a lab that lays the abort loop bare (live iteration count, per-attempt rejection reasons, the sparse ±1 challenge, and the response histogram) — plus HashML-DSA (the FIPS 204 §5.4 pre-hash mode over SHA-512 or SHAKE-256, cryptographically bound to its hash's DER OID), deterministic-vs-hedged signing, and a rejection-loop iteration histogram. A SECURE-COMPUTATION lab opens a whole new pillar — computing on inputs two parties never share — with Yao's two-party protocol built from scratch: a Chou–Orlandi oblivious transfer on this lab's Ed25519 group (the sender never learns the receiver's choice; the receiver opens only one message), then garbled circuits with the free-XOR and half-gate optimizations (XOR and NOT are free; an AND costs the proven-minimal two ciphertexts) over 128-bit labels from the lab's own SHA-256. It runs Yao's original Millionaires' Problem — who is richer, revealing nothing else — plus private equality, sum, product, and a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction — learn the winner and the price, never the bids — each with an auditable transcript and a live single-byte-tamper integrity demo, verified exhaustively against a plaintext oracle over every 4-bit input pair; and, as a second paradigm on the same circuits, the GMW protocol (secret sharing instead of garbling — wires kept XOR-shared, each AND gate resolved by a 1-of-4 oblivious transfer), cross-checked to reconstruct the identical result. A VERIFIABLE DELAY FUNCTION lab adds the time analogue of the VRF — proof of *sequential* work: y = x^(2^T) mod N over a 512-bit Blum RSA group takes T squarings that no parallelism can shorten, yet verifies in one shot via BOTH the succinct Wesolowski proof (a single group element and a Fiat–Shamir hash-to-prime ℓ, checked by π^ℓ·x^r = y) and the log-size Pietrzak halving proof (a recursive fold down to y = x², log₂T midpoints), each pinned against the trapdoor evaluation (e = 2^T mod φ(N), the shortcut that is exactly why a real modulus must be one nobody has factored — an RSA challenge number or a class group) and against forged proofs, mauled outputs, and the wrong delay — plus a Rivest–Shamir–Wagner time-lock puzzle that encrypts a message to the future (locked instantly with the trapdoor, opened only by grinding the full squaring chain live) and an unbiasable delay-based randomness beacon that chains VDF outputs each carrying a verifiable proof-of-time (the RANDAO+VDF / Chia proof-of-time shape). A companion CLASS-GROUP VDF closes the RSA construction's one gap — its trapdoor — by moving the whole Wesolowski machine into the CLASS GROUP OF AN IMAGINARY QUADRATIC ORDER Cl(Δ), a group of genuinely UNKNOWN ORDER WITH NO TRUSTED SETUP (the class number h(Δ) ≈ √|Δ| is believed as hard as factoring to compute, and Δ is just a public prime discriminant hashed from a seed, so unlike an RSA modulus nobody — not even its creator — holds a φ to shortcut the delay): binary quadratic forms (a,b,c) built from scratch on BigInt with Gauss reduction (the ρ operator, coordinates bounded by √(|Δ|/3) forever) and Gauss composition (Cohen Alg. 5.4.7), a canonical prime-form generator, y = g^(2^T) by T sequential class-group squarings, the one-form succinct proof π = g^⌊2^T/ℓ⌋ verified by π^ℓ ∘ g^r = y, an O(1)-memory streaming prover, and a no-trusted-setup delay beacon — the engine under Chia's consensus, validated against the group axioms on the FULL CAYLEY TABLE of small discriminants and the known class numbers h(−23)=3, h(−47)=5, h(−71)=7, h(−3299)=27. A DOUBLY-EFFICIENT INTERACTIVE-PROOF lab implements the SUM-CHECK PROTOCOL and GKR from scratch over the Goldilocks field — multilinear extensions and the ẽq Lagrange basis, the round-by-round univariate messages a verifier collapses with a single oracle evaluation instead of an exponential sum, and a Fiat–Shamir transcript — then layers it into the Goldwasser–Kalai–Rothblum protocol that certifies a whole layered arithmetic circuit's output while the verifier re-executes ZERO gates, reducing each layer to the next by one sum-check fused with the two-claim line-restriction trick and bottoming out at the public input's MLE; alongside the two canonical applications — verified n×n MATRIX MULTIPLICATION (check C = A·B from O(log n) interaction, never redoing the O(n³) product; Thaler §4.4) and TRIANGLE COUNTING (proving Σ Ã(x,y)Ã(y,z)Ã(z,x) = 6·#triangles with the adjacency MLE evaluated at just three points) — the interactive-proof machinery under Spartan, HyperPlonk and Jolt, with live soundness demos that catch a forged claimed sum, a forged product entry, an inflated triangle count, or a single tampered output wire. A capstone BALLOT lab finally wires the threshold and zero-knowledge shelves into the protocol they were invented for — HELIOS/BELENIOS end-to-end-VERIFIABLE VOTING, built entirely from the lab's own parts: EXPONENTIAL ELGAMAL on secp256k1 whose ciphertexts are ADDITIVELY HOMOMORPHIC (votes encoded in the exponent so a bulletin board tallies encrypted ballots and decrypts only the total, recovered by a bounded baby-step giant-step discrete log), a PEDERSEN (joint-Feldman) DISTRIBUTED KEY GENERATION that splits the decryption key t-of-n so no authority can decrypt, 1-of-k ballots each carrying a DISJUNCTIVE CHAUM–PEDERSEN proof that every slot encrypts a bit plus a DLEQ that the slots sum to exactly one vote (cast-as-intended, no ballot-stuffing), a homomorphic tally, THRESHOLD DECRYPTION where each trustee publishes a partial decryption with a DLEQ proof and any t combine by Lagrange in the exponent, and — the property real elections are graded on — a UNIVERSAL VERIFIER that re-derives the trustee keys from the public commitments and re-checks every ballot and decryption proof trusting no one and touching no secret, with live tamper toggles (ballot-stuffing, a dishonest trustee) it catches by name. A BBS ANONYMOUS-CREDENTIALS lab adds the multi-message signature the digital-identity world is standardising on (draft-irtf-cfrg-bbs-signatures — the crypto under W3C Verifiable Credentials, the ISO mobile driver's licence, and the EU Digital Identity Wallet), built from scratch on the lab's own BLS12-381 pairing: an issuer signs a VECTOR of attributes once (A = (P1 + domain·Q₁ + Σ mᵢ·Hᵢ)/(sk+e), verified by one pairing e(A, PK+e·P₂) = e(B, P₂)), and the holder later proves possession of that signature in ZERO KNOWLEDGE while DISCLOSING ONLY A CHOSEN SUBSET of attributes — a Fiat–Shamir Σ-proof over a randomized signature (Ā = r·A, D̂ = r·B − e·Ā, with the pairing e(Ā, PK) = e(D̂, P₂) surviving the randomization) that hides every undisclosed message and makes every presentation UNLINKABLE to every other, so a mobile driver's licence can prove OVER-21 to a bar without revealing name, date of birth, or the licence number that would let two bars recognise you, all with the issuer offline — with a live lab (disclose/hide toggles, an editable verifier session that catches replay, and a soundness panel that rejects a lied-about value, a tampered Ā, and a mauled response) and a soundness argument that extracts a genuine signature from any accepting proof. All computed live in the browser, pinned to published test vectors, with zero crypto dependencies.
